How fast is GitTurtle?

Time to the first window, a selected commit’s changed files, a prepared diff, and monorepo backend pipelines measured in release builds on real hardware.

115 ms to the first window

On an Apple M2 Pro running Omarchy Linux and Hyprland on Wayland, the median of nine warm launches was 115 ms. The timer started when the executable ran and stopped when the compositor mapped its window. The fastest launch took 103 ms and the slowest took 135 ms.

The October 27, 2026 Linux interface-font check alternated two release builds against the same demo repository. Each launch started with fresh app settings and a warm system cache. A cold launch, or time to load every part of a repository, measures a different operation.

From a commit to a diff

Native history interactions, in milliseconds
OperationMedian95th percentile
Select commit → changed files ready21.245.2
Open text file → history diff ready4.97.4

The September 8, 2026 run used a release app at commit f68bd20 on an Apple M4 Max with 128 GiB RAM and macOS 26.6.2. The fixture had 653 commits. Each row covers twenty deliberate selections, ten steps down and ten back. Revisiting a file could reuse its cached preview.

Timing started in the input handler and finished when the prepared result reached the app. Input delivery, display presentation and completed GPU work fall outside this interval. The median is the middle of the samples. The 95th percentile gives a sense of the slower selections.

Paging and scrolling long histories

  • 0.525 ms per subsequent page. In a 120,000-commit linear history, a warm backend benchmark loaded each further 500-commit page in a median of 0.525 ms, with a 95th percentile of 0.568 ms. The first 500 took 429 ms. This September 10 run on an M4 Max visited 100,000 commits per pass and excluded drawing the rows.
  • 8.15 ms of UI-thread CPU per wheel notch. In a 1,480 × 800 History window on an M2 Pro running Omarchy, the October 27 release build 0aca11e scrolled a 3,000-commit fixture backed by memory. Across six launches, the 95th percentile was 13.17 ms. This measures CPU work for a scroll step. It is a different quantity from a frame’s time on screen.

Core Git and monorepo pipelines (November 2026)

In November 2026, two same-session alternating --release benchmark rounds on an Apple M2 Pro running Omarchy Linux (pinned to P-cores 4–11) measured backend and preview-pipeline improvements across a 500-commit repository, a 12,000-file repository, a 4,000-commit search fixture and a 16 MiB PDF helper transfer.

Alongside those measured backend latencies, GitTurtle now separates fast metadata reads from heavy preview decoding across a bounded two-lane worker, collapses giant untracked trees under a fixed probe budget (reducing a 12,000-file untracked node_modules/ scan from 12,003 rows to 4), degrades monorepo local watching to Git metadata directories cleanly, avoids duplicating RGBA pixel buffers during image decoding, defers split-diff and Settings UI construction until needed, and draws straight commit-graph lanes as snapped quads. These backend figures exclude live compositor presentation and are recorded in full under docs/benchmarks/ in the repository.

Current-build release check (November 24, 2026)

After shrinking the release binary (106.8 MiB raw ELF / 32.4 MiB packaged tarball on Linux ARM64, down 25.3% from 142.9 MiB with all 28 Tree-sitter grammars and preview formats intact), adding Shift-click range compare and rebase drag-reorder, and hardening Linux IME and AT-SPI accessibility, clean release build 07a1492d was measured on Apple M2 Pro P-cores (4–11) under a quiet host lock.

With no screen reader active, accessible text-run hooks (without D-Bus or paint) measured a pooled median of 0.083 µs across 6,600 samples spanning fixtures up to 5 MB / 100,000 lines (0.083–0.084 µs per-series median, 4.750 µs max); with a screen reader active, cached redraws took 0.71 µs for an input, 7.21 µs for a 2 KB text area and 1.252 ms for a 5 MB (100,000-line) editor. Headless GPUI rows run on GPUI’s test platform and exclude font shaping, GPU execution and compositor presentation; live compositor launch and scroll figures remain anchored to their dated records above.

Measurement records

Read the summaries or download the raw samples for both the current-build refresh and the original GUI and pagination measurements. Each CSV contains the recorded values in collection order.

  • November 24 current-build release summary (text) records the 07a1492d binary footprint, core Git, worker, app CPU and headless GPUI timings on M2 Pro P-cores.
  • November 24 500-commit page timings (CSV) gives all 600 incremental page reads from the 07a1492d 120,000-commit linear-history run.
  • Warm-launch timing summary (text) includes the base and candidate medians and ranges from the October 27 interface-font check.
  • Commit selection and text-diff timings (CSV) pairs the two September 8 navigation sequences by selection number, with 20 elapsed times for each operation.
  • September 10 500-commit page timings (CSV) gives all 600 incremental page reads from the original M4 Max linear-history benchmark. Filter out offset zero to reproduce the subsequent-page result.
  • UI-thread CPU time per wheel notch (CSV) gives all 720 measured notches from the six wide-window launches of 0aca11e in the October 27 quiet-host run.
